items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: And then I grabbed Steve Swallow, because he used to work at this club in the Village where I worked a couple of nights a week and on Monday nights he’d come in and play, and I started doing the things with him and then every once in a while we’d do a little date together.

ctx.x: Yeah, exactly one step, right. But I remember that. And then I grabbed Steve Swallow, because he used to work at this club in the Village where I worked a couple of nights a week and on Monday nights he’d come in and play, and I started doing the things with him and then every once in a while we’d do a little date together. There was a club in the Village that did a lot of sort of avante garde type music called the Take Three, and it was upstairs. And we would go up there, carry the bass up there and do this…

wonderful. Yeah. And I’ve been doing it ever since. It’s just that now I’ve gotten back together with Cameron Brown. Because originally he had rehearsed bass and voice with me but then he got very busy with some of the other musicians you know. And he couldn’t rehearse as much. And then Harvey of course came in to the picture from the Steve Kuhn Quartet.

items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And then, uh, I also was on a Steve Swallow recording of Robert Creeley poetry called Home.

ctx.x: Don Cherry. Uh, well, you there was a long association that helped bring your name to maybe a second generation after the sixties into the late seventies, early eighties when you teamed up with Harvey, Harvey S. Talk a little bit, little bit about that, that, how that came to be.

Yeah. I‟m not gonna go into detail about that because, you know, we talked about it a little bit off-camera. So I‟m just gonna say that, uh, I… for some reason, I got hooked on the bass a long time ago. I heard it. Now maybe in another life I was a bass player. I don‟t know. But I loved the bass. I love singing with the bass. And I used to sing with Swallow every chance I got at the Page Three to try out some things. Of course, the piano player would get all bent out of shape. But uh, I was with Steve Kuhn‟s…
